page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual machine powered by AWS Graviton4 silicon built on the arm64 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture. The instance is assigned a single dedicated physical core running at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, alongside 2.0 GB of memory and a bundled 59 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage volume. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform.

Benchmark results reflect the balance between single-core Graviton4 processing capability and the constraints of a single-core envelope. The instance achieves strong results in single-threaded decompression tasks, with bzip3 reaching 14.06 GB/sec, placing it in the upper quartile of evaluated systems. General compute stress testing via stress-ng registers 1692.09 points in both single-core and overall evaluations, while gzip compression achieves an average 30.06 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput, PassMark aggregate scores, and large memory copy operations place in lower percentiles due to the single-vCPU ceiling and 2.0 GB memory boundary.

From an infrastructure and efficiency perspective, c8gd.medium provides a cost-effective development and edge processing target for ARM-native software stacks that require high-speed local scratch disk space. The inclusion of low-latency direct-attached NVMe storage eliminates external volume overhead for temporary artifacts, though the 2.0 GB RAM footprint limits concurrency. It is suited for single-threaded microservices, lightweight web serving, local caching tiers, log buffering, and continuous integration testing targeting ARM64.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.medium is a compute-optimized arm64 instance powered by a single dedicated AWS Graviton4 Neoverse-V2 core operating at 2.8 GHz. The server configuration includes 2.0 GB of system memory, 1 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, and a bundled 59 GB local NVMe SSD instance store on the AWS Nitro System. Single-threaded performance benchmarks demonstrate competitive integer and compression capabilities, led by a strong bzip3 decompression throughput of 14.06 GB/sec and average gzip compression at 30.06 GB/sec. Overall multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth are bounded by the single-thread allocation and 2.0 GB memory capacity. Without an attached GPU, this instance represents a resource-efficient platform for running lightweight microservices, isolated build agents, local caching layers, and entry-level container workloads that benefit from direct NVMe scratch storage and dedicated 64-bit ARM compute.
